item.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening arises from the atomic size difference among the six principal alloying elements in the equiatomic BCC matrix.
item.system: Equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (HEA) with a BCC1 matrix phase
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature compressive testing; consolidated by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 1400 °C for 10 min under 30 MPa
item.supporting_observation: The authors attribute the excellent mechanical properties to solid solution strengthening caused by atomic size differences, alongside grain boundary and precipitation strengthening.
item.scope_limits: Not explicitly tested for alloys with non-equiatomic ratios or different element sets; the text notes high-entropy theory may not apply to materials with very large heats of formation like oxides.
item.alternatives_considered: Ordered phases or intermetallic compounds (which traditional theory predicts for multi-element alloys) are not formed in the solid solution matrix.
quotes: The excellent mechanical properties can be attributed to solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening of the fine-grained BCC matrix
It should be noted that the solid solution strengthening caused by atomic size difference of alloying elements in the HEA also contributes to the excellent mechanical properties
Yeh et al. [ [1] ] have pointed out that the high-entropy theory does not apply to materials with very large heats of formation, such as oxides, carbides, and nitrides

item.mechanism: Grain boundary strengthening occurs due to the refinement of the BCC matrix grains to an average size of 1.35 μm, which impedes dislocation motion.
item.system: Equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi refractory HEA consolidated by SPS
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature; sintered at 1400 °C for 10 min under 30 MPa; compared to as-cast HEA with tens of microns grain size
item.supporting_observation: The fine equiaxed BCC matrix grains (1.35 μm) lead to a strong grain boundary strengthening effect compared to coarse dendrite grains in as-cast HEA.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the fine-grained microstructure produced by mechanical alloying and SPS; not applicable to coarse-grained as-cast microstructures.
item.alternatives_considered: Coarse dendritic segregation and large grain sizes typical of vacuum arc-melting methods.
quotes: Compared with the coarse dendrite grains with the average grain size of tens of microns in the as-cast HEA, the equiaxed BCC matrix grains with the average grain size of 1.35 μm in the present work is much finer, therefore leading to a strong grain boundary strengthening effect
The average grain size of BCC matrix phase and TiO are measured to be 1.35 μm and 0.46 μm, respectively
Mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering is a promising way to further improve mechanical properties of the refractory HEA by means of grain refinement

item.mechanism: Precipitation strengthening is provided by fine TiO particles (FCC phase) that impede dislocation motion within the BCC matrix.
item.system: NbMoTaWVTi HEA containing TiO precipitates formed during SPS
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature compression; TiO formed during SPS at 1400 °C and rapid cooling; oxygen content in powders was 0.86 mass %
item.supporting_observation: The precipitated fine TiO particles are likely to impede dislocation motion, increasing strength while slightly decreasing ductility.
item.scope_limits: Dependent on the presence of oxygen introduced during mechanical alloying; the mechanism relies on the formation of TiO specifically.
item.alternatives_considered: Other interstitial elements like N could form precipitates, but TiO is the specific phase observed here due to Ti's high oxygen affinity.
quotes: The precipitated fine TiO particles are likely to impede the dislocation motion in the BCC matrix, thus increasing strength and slightly decreasing the ductility of the alloy, simultaneously
The FCC precipitated phase is identified as TiO, due to the introduction of O during the preparing process of HEA
There is a high probability that oxygen may be brought into the HEA during the MA process

item.mechanism: A new FCC phase precipitates from the original BCC phase during the heating process of mechanical alloying powders, specifically above 900 °C.
item.system: NbMoTaWVTi HEA powders after 40 h of ball milling
item.operating_conditions: Heating at 900 °C for 1 h or SPS at 1400 °C; DSC analysis shows exothermic peak at 707.5 °C
item.supporting_observation: New diffraction peaks characterized as FCC structures are observed in powders heated at 900 °C and in the consolidated bulk HEA, but not at 500 °C.
item.scope_limits: The phase transition does not occur below 900 °C; the FCC structure is retained due to rapid cooling after SPS.
item.alternatives_considered: No phase transition occurs at 500 °C; the BCC structure remains stable at lower temperatures.
quotes: Figure 1 d presents the DSC curve that an exothermic peak is obviously observed at 707.5 °C

The XRD pattern of powders after heating at 500 °C is nearly the same as the original powders, while new diffraction peaks, characterized as face-centered cubic (FCC) structures, are observed both in powders heated at 900 °C and consolidated bulk HEA
It is reasonable to conclude that a new FCC phase precipitates from original BCC phases during the SPS process

item.mechanism: A minor BCC2 phase forms at grain boundaries due to the slightly inhomogeneous distribution of alloying elements (depleted in W, Mo, Ta) during sintering.
item.system: NbMoTaWVTi HEA bulk material with grain boundaries
item.operating_conditions: After SPS at 1400 °C for 10 min under 30 MPa; observed in bulk sintered sample
item.supporting_observation: Line scanning shows the BCC2 phase composition is close to BCC1 but slightly depleted of W, Mo, and Ta, suggesting inhomogeneous distribution.
item.scope_limits: The phase is too small (60~250 nm thickness) for direct EDS quantitative analysis; its formation is speculative based on elemental gradients.
item.alternatives_considered: The phase could be a result of segregation rather than a distinct thermodynamic phase, but is treated as a distinct BCC2 phase.
quotes: It can be speculated that the formation of BCC2 results from the slightly inhomogeneous distribution of alloying elements at the grain boundaries of sintered HEA
The results shown in Figure 2 b indicate that the chemical composition of BCC2 phase is close to BCC1, except that it is slightly depleted of W, Mo, and Ta
The thickness of BCC2 phase is measured to be about 60~250 nm, and the volume fraction of BCC2 is estimated to be about 3%

item.mechanism: The FCC TiO phase retains its high-temperature crystal structure due to the rapid cooling rate after SPS, preventing transformation to monoclinic structure.
item.operating_conditions: SPS at 1400 °C followed by cooling at 300 °C/min to 500 °C and then slow cooling to ambient
item.supporting_observation: The presence of FCC TiO at ambient temperature is attributed to the rapid cooling speed after SPS, as TiO is normally monoclinic at ambient temperature.
item.scope_limits: Relies on the specific cooling rate of the SPS process; slower cooling might allow transformation to monoclinic TiO.
item.alternatives_considered: Transformation to monoclinic crystal structure which is the stable form at ambient temperature.
quotes: TiO has an FCC structure at elevated temperature and a monoclinic crystal structure at ambient temperature

The formation of TiO phase with FCC structure in the sintered sample indicated that the TiO phase remains in its original crystal structure at elevated temperature, due to the rapid cooling speed after SPS
The FCC precipitated phase is identified as TiO, due to the introduction of O during the preparing process of HEA

item.mechanism: The introduction of interstitial oxygen during mechanical alloying leads to the formation of oxide precipitates (TiO) which enhance strength.
item.system: NbMoTaWVTi HEA prepared by mechanical alloying and SPS
item.operating_conditions: Mechanical alloying for 40 h in argon atmosphere; oxygen content measured at 0.86 mass % in milled powders
item.supporting_observation: The mass fraction of oxygen in the powders after 40 h of milling is measured to be 0.86%, and Ti has a much higher oxygen affinity than other elements.
item.scope_limits: Specific to alloys containing Ti and oxygen; the mechanism depends on the presence of interstitial elements introduced during processing.
item.alternatives_considered: Other interstitial elements like N could be introduced, but TiO formation is dominant due to Ti's affinity.
quotes: It is inevitable that interstitial elements, such as O, N, etc. will be introduced during the preparing process, which will lead to the formation of precipitated phases
The mass fraction of oxygen in the powders after 40 h of milling is measured to be 0.86%
It is apparent that Ti has a much higher oxygen affinity than other alloying elements, therefore leading to the formation of TiO phase

item.mechanism: The combination of plastic and brittle fracture mechanisms results in a fracture surface with both flat/smeared areas (shear tearing) and intergranular fracture areas.
item.system: NbMoTaWVTi HEA bulk material under compressive loading
item.operating_conditions: Compressive test at room temperature with strain rate of 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹; fracture strain of 11.4%
item.supporting_observation: Fracture morphologies show flat and smeared areas from shear tearing and intergranular fracture areas with fine particles on grain boundaries.
item.scope_limits: Observed at room temperature; the balance between plastic and brittle behavior may change at elevated temperatures.
item.alternatives_considered: Purely ductile or purely brittle fracture modes; the observed mode is a combination.
quotes: There are two types of morphologies in the fracture surface: flat and smeared area, as a result of shear tearing, and intergranular fracture area, with some fine particles dispersed on the grain boundaries, indicating a combination of plastic and brittle fracture mechanisms
The alloy exhibits compressive yield strength of 2709 MPa, fracture strength of 3115 MPa, and total fracture strain of 11.4% at ambient temperature
Figure 4 c,d shows fracture morphologies of NbMoTaWVTi HEA at different magnifications
